headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and medium prompt-injection/cascade exposure; no direct evidence of a critical compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and marketingskills explicitly uses shared skill/context files that reference each other. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if one agent writes content the other later treats as trusted. The pairwise interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_b writes instructions into shared skill/context files that agent_a later ingests
IF agent_a parses file content as actionable instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Make shared files read-only for one agent
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's output
Prefix untrusted content with a non-executable marker
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have filesystem access, but the profiles do not show sensitive data classes, shared OAuth, or uncontrolled third-party uploads. AutoGPT has allowlisted egress and marketingskills is docs-only with marketing context, so leakage is possible mainly through a shared workspace rather than obvious exfiltration. That keeps the blast radius limited and the evidence weak.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing confidential files
IF either agent is configured to read those files into its context
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Remove confidential files from any shared directory
Restrict file permissions so only one agent can read sensitive folders
Review allowlisted egress destinations
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and marketingskills can read and write the filesystem while also spawning subprocesses. Because both can mutate files and run concurrently, the shared-dir conflict pathway is plausible in default use and can corrupt work products or state. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF either agent modifies files without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Disable write access for one agent where possible
Run only one agent at a time on shared state
Use file locks around mutable artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around shared context and reference chaining, while AutoGPT can generate and act on outputs from files and shell steps. If AutoGPT-produced content is fed into marketingskills without verification, errors can propagate into downstream marketing artifacts. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes AutoGPT output as authoritative context
IF no human or automated verification step checks the intermediate result
mitigations: Insert a review step between agents
Require source citations for any factual claims
Limit AutoGPT output to drafts only
Compare outputs against a checklist before reuse
requires-engineering: add validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile. AutoGPT is open-source and marketingskills is docs-only marketing tooling, so there is no direct evidence of a compliance breach pathway. Because the profiles are sparse and unverified, I keep a low residual risk rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workspace
IF the deployment environment imposes residency or retention rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention and deletion rules
Review deployment residency settings
Use separate logs for each agent
requires-engineering: map data flows to compliance controls
